description:
ABOUT ARCHITECT LABS

Architect Labs is advancing new frontiers in AI through silicon. Our goal is to compress end-to-end software to silicon timelines, and maximize intelligence per watt and per dollar for the world. Achieving this requires us to not only build our own radically competitive silicon products, but also reimagine how they are discovered, designed and produced at scale. We are a small exceptional team across silicon, systems, software and frontier AI. Our team has led research teams at nearly every frontier AI labs, and taped out some of the most complex SoCs in the world.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

A placer finishes twice as fast. The router spends the afternoon undoing its choices. Did the new algorithm buy us anything? You’ll have the blocks, the implementation flow, and the freedom to answer that question. Your job is to invent or accelerate physical design flows, tools and algorithms to change how we build chips end to end with AI, with focus on Place, Route, Clock tree, Synthesis, Hand off to Backend, power/timing estimations and over physical convergence.

 - Choose the research problem: Identify, analyze and size every bottleneck with the physical design team, prioritize them and solve every one. It might be congestion that only becomes visible after routing, or a timing update expensive enough to rule out an otherwise promising search strategy.

 - Build the solver: Own the algorithm, the flow, measurement and its implementation. That could mean a better objective for placement, an incremental graph update, or a parallel routing kernel. Profile it on real netlists and use what you learn to choose the next experiment.

 - Benchmark the full flow: Give the incumbent tool a fair run. Match constraints and compute budgets, then follow the result through routing. Measure elapsed time, slack, area, and routability, including on the blocks where your method loses.

 - Put the algorithm/flow into production: Work alongside the engineer closing the block. Make the solver reproducible, diagnose the corner cases together, and put it into the flow when the gains hold up.


WHAT WE'D LIKE TO SEE

Qualifications & Skills:

 - Algorithm development: You’ve implemented an algorithm for placement, routing, timing, or a related EDA problem. A dissertation, open-source tool, or commercial product can all demonstrate that experience.

 - Implementation depth: You write performance-sensitive code and can explain how your choice of data structures or numerical methods affected runtime, memory use, and solution quality on larger designs.

 - Experimental judgment: You design reproducible comparisons against strong baselines and can describe a case where a promising result failed to hold up downstream.The typo fixes from the last round (cover date, “Agrani Labs wins”, the double space) are still in place.

 - GPU Acceleration: Experience accelerating placement, routing, or timing analysis with incremental methods or GPU parallelism.

 - AI for Physical Design: Worked on numerical optimization, combinatorial solvers, or learned cost models for physical design.

Bonus:

 - Experience working on industry standard tool development for Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens, etc - especially on digital physical design space.

 - Experience working on research teams focused on AI for chip design, GPU-accelerated EDA tools for physical design etc.


WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive compensation, equity, and the opportunity to work on new tools, and methodologies to advance AI-driven physical design.
